title: Work Passes Issued under Manpower for Strategic Economic Priorities Scheme
what_it_is: Work Passes Issued under Manpower for Strategic Economic Priorities Scheme

sections.label: M-SEP questions to Minister
sections.summary: Questions ask the Minister for Trade and Industry about M-SEP pass numbers, eligibility, deployment, training, PMETs, safeguards, local impact and firms under investigation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry (a) what is the expected number of additional S Passes and Work Permits to be issued under the Manpower for Strategic Economic Priorities (M-SEP) scheme; (b) whether smaller companies and outsourced service providers that support the strategic economic priorities can also be eligible; and (c) how will the Ministry ascertain that the additional foreign workers obtained under the scheme will be deployed in areas that advance Singapore's economic goals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry (a) how will the Ministry ensure the relevance of skills and employability of workers who are sent for training under Condition 2 of the M-SEP scheme; and (b) whether the required hiring and training under this scheme can have a greater focus and emphasis on mid-career PMETs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry (a) how will the M-SEP scheme benefit Singaporean PMEs and workers; and (b) what are the safeguards against abuse of work passes issued under this scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry (a) what is the projected impact of the M-SEP scheme on locals, in terms of wages and job opportunities; (b) what are the steps which the Ministry will be taking to ensure a level playing field for local workers; and (c) whether companies under investigation by the Ministry for poor employment practices or firms that have breached the Fair Consideration Framework, or the Tripartite Guidelines on Fair Employment Practices, will be eligible for the M-SEP scheme.

sections.label: M-SEP scheme and qualifying priorities
sections.summary: The scheme lets qualifying firms temporarily hire S Pass and Work Permit holders above the DRC and S Pass sub-DRC if they meet key economic priorities.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Specifically, the scheme gives qualifying firms the flexibility to temporarily hire S Pass and Work Permit holders above the prevailing Dependency Ratio Ceiling, or DRC, and S Pass sub-DRC.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: To qualify, firms must participate in programmes or activities in line with one of the following key economic priorities, namely: one, investments that support Singapore's hub strategy; two, innovation or research and development (R&D); or three, internationalisation.

sections.label: Number of qualifying firms
sections.summary: Only about 1,000 firms will meet the qualifying criteria, less than 1% of all registered business entities in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Only about 1,000 firms will meet the qualifying criteria.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: This represents less than 1% of all registered business entities in Singapore.

sections.label: Hiring commitments and local salary
sections.summary: Firms can hire local workers through their own channels or Government programmes if paid above the Local Qualifying Salary of $1,400.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: On hiring commitments, firms can choose to hire local workers through their own channels or through Government programmes, as long as these locals are paid above the Local Qualifying Salary (LQS) of $1,400.

sections.label: Maintaining local workforce share
sections.summary: All M-SEP firms must minimally maintain their local workforce share during the support period, though not all eligible firms may need support.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Regardless of whether firms choose to meet Condition 2 through hiring or training commitments, all M-SEP firms will also need to minimally maintain their local workforce share during the M-SEP support period.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: While there are around 1,000 firms that are eligible under Condition 1, not all may require M-SEP support.

sections.label: Breaches bar M-SEP benefits
sections.summary: Firms that breached the FCF or TGFEP may be barred from work pass privileges and cannot benefit from M-SEP.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Firms that have breached the Fair Consideration Framework (FCF) or the Tripartite Guidelines on Fair Employment Practices (TGFEP) may be barred from work pass privileges and will not be able to benefit from M-SEP.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: As Members would be aware, we are taking a very significant step forward of enshrining the TGFEP in law and we will share more details in due course.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We will take reference from the penalty framework of the new legislation when deciding on the treatment of such firms.

sections.label: M-SEP objectives and eligibility
sections.summary: M-SEP creates hiring or training opportunities directly and supports strategic economic priorities indirectly through growth of needle-moving companies, with 1,000 companies eligible.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: M-SEP will do so in two ways: directly, through the creation of hiring or training opportunities; and more significantly, indirectly, through the growth of needle-moving companies which support our strategic economic priorities.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Designed with these principal objectives in mind, M-SEP will strengthen our competitiveness.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The Government will continue to monitor the outcomes of the M-SEP scheme and will enable us to generate economic opportunities and provide better outcomes for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: We have Condition 1 and Condition 2, and more and more to assess whether it can fit into that and other criteria.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: He mentioned that there are 1,000 companies eligible for M-SEP.

sections.label: M-SEP key success factor
sections.summary: The key success factor for the M-SEP scheme are the economic outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The key success factor for the M-SEP scheme are the economic outcomes.

sections.label: SMEs and known firms
sections.summary: Helping more SMEs is at a very early stage, and the 1,000 firms are already well known to agencies including EDB, ESG, STB, IMDA and MPA.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: With regard to helping and widening it for more SMEs, we are at a very early stage in terms of working with many of the firms.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: These 1,000 firms that we talked about, they are already very well known to the agencies that I mentioned earlier on – EDB, ESG, STB, IMDA, MPA, amongst others.

sections.label: Initial step training hiring
sections.summary: The initial landmark step is to increase the number of training opportunities and hiring opportunities for locals.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Indeed, in the initial step – which is quite a landmark step – the plan is to increase the number of training opportunities and the hiring opportunities for our locals.

sections.label: Sixteen policies for SMEs
sections.summary: A list of 16 policies is incorporated so SMEs can see how to leverage and tap on them to benefit from the scheme.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: What we have incorporated in these small steps are a list of 16 policies that SMEs can look and see how they can leverage on these 16 policies and tap on them to move forward and be able to benefit from the scheme.

sections.label: M-SEP not a U-turn
sections.summary: With regard to M-SEP, it is not a "U-turn".

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: With regard to M-SEP, it is not a "U-turn".

sections.label: Extending M-SEP to audit firms
sections.summary: Extending M-SEP to audit firms would be too broad-based and run counter to the highly selective scheme, though firms can work with WSG and SSG.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Today, by extension, if you want to extend the M-SEP support scheme to audit firms, I think it would really be too broad-based and it may run counter to M-SEP, which is intended to be very highly selective.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Today, audit firms and professional companies can work with WSG and SSG to see how we can help them to scale up our locals to meet their manpower needs.

sections.label: Unanswered U-turn question
sections.summary: A Member's question on whether it is a U-turn has not been answered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The second question is that you have not answered our fellow Member Leon Perera's question on whether it is a "U-turn" or not.

sections.label: Monitoring 30% ratio and M-SEP
sections.summary: The 30% ratio will be monitored closely, and M-SEP's selective nature and stringent criteria mean numbers are not expected to affect the proportion significantly.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: For the record, for the 30% ratio, we will continue to monitor this very closely.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: But the M-SEP, because of the very highly selective nature of the scheme and because of the stringent criteria that we have applied for Condition 1 and Condition 2, we do not expect, in the penultimate, the numbers to affect the proportion significantly.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Please remember, Mr Leong, that the M-SEP is here to help us generate more economic opportunities for Singaporeans, because in the second condition, it is about making sure that there are more training opportunities for Singaporeans and the jobs for Singaporeans.
